name: Network Denial of Service
summary: Adversaries may perform Network Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to users. Network DoS can be performed by exhausting the network bandwidth that services rely on, or by jamming the signal going to or coming from devices. A Network DoS will occur when an adversary is able to jam radio signals (e.g. Wi-Fi, cellular, GPS) around a device to prevent it from communicating. For example, to jam…

strategies.name: Detection of Network Denial of Service

analytics.name: Analytic 1713
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Network Denial of Service by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Application Permission via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]; OS API Execution via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: ConnectivityManager, TelephonyManager, or WifiManager framework callbacks report repeated failure, disable, or oscillation events outside expected coverage-transition pattern]; Protected Configuration via…

analytics.name: Analytic 1714
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Network Denial of Service from documented management, network, or vetting evidence; treat state queries as periodic observations rather than real-time events. Correlate Application State via Apple MDM [InstalledApplicationList / ManagedApplicationList]; Protected Configuration via Apple MDM [DeviceInformation / SecurityInfo / ProfileList / restrictions and compliance queries]; System Settings via Apple MDM [DeviceInformation / SecurityInfo / ProfileList / restrictions and compliance queries].
